entry.title: Social Summary: September 24, 2026
entry.summary:
Bot Screen & Live Desktop Launch (dominant story): The week belonged to the Bot Screen debut in Hermes Desktop. @NousResearch's official launch post introduced real-time streaming of any bot session so users can watch agents drive a browser or terminal live, while co-founder @Teknium's companion announcement of visual + interactive passthrough to the same machine a Hermes Agent is controlling was the community's biggest post at ~1,046 likes. @tonbistudio produced the walkthrough video, with the official account sharing docs at a strong 488 likes and Teknium amplifying it further. Sentiment was strongly positive and clearly anticipatory — Teknium's 'Finallllly!' (69 likes / 4.3k views) and 'Much needed!' (189 likes / 18.6k views) suggest this was one of the most requested Hermes capabilities, with 'Impressive!' reactions to community demos rounding out the excitement.

oh-my-hermes Plugin & JEV Tooling: @rlaope had a productive week: open-sourcing jeval for JEV model evaluation and visualization plus an oh-my-hermes update adding JEV skills and model routing (models/aliases, skills/plugins, workflow decisions), and positioning OMH as the 'all-in-one plugin for AI-native' Hermes Agent users. A condensed re-share of jeval was demoted as a near-duplicate of the fuller release post.

Maintainer Responsiveness & Attribution: Founders stayed hands-on in the replies. @Teknium pushed back on a claimed cache bug and asked for a reproducible issue path — confident but showing minor friction — confirmed a fast fix after user feedback, and corrected misattribution by clarifying a circulating tool was built by NousResearch, not Anthropic. Overall read: responsive, opinionated maintainership.

Usage Tips: A practical official tip that users can run Hermes via iMessage with any model they choose drew solid engagement, and community reaction to the new guide video was warm if casual.

Filtered as noise: Emoji-only and one-word hype replies (🔥, 😭, 'I agree', 'This is the way'), a bare OMH link re-post, a generic 'drop your GitHub' engagement prompt, and vague off-topic chatter about Claude Opus 5.5 (GA 2026-09-22) and Claude Code were excluded from the ranked list for lack of informational value.
